notes: Prompts stay short and withhold detail on purpose — a user doesn't narrate a session back to the agent that was in it, and a prompt containing every fact lets the model skip step 1's scoping. Prior state a case depends on is described in expected_output as a precondition, not put in the user's mouth. Eval 1 is the core case and the one that distinguishes this skill from `distill-lessons`: the work taught nothing, so a lessons pass correctly produces nothing, and this pass must still find the falsified status line. It needs a seeded store containing a record that calls the work unmerged. Eval 2 guards the most destructive failure mode — deleting a dated historical statement because it reads like a stale one. Eval 3 is a near-miss that belongs to `distill-lessons`, not here. Eval 4 tests the deletion bar: the surviving copy must make the same claim, not merely contain the same words. Eval 5 covers gate five, the only gate with nothing stale to find: every other gate returns empty, so a shallow pass produces a clean bill of health and loses the state. It pairs with eval 1 — same 'nothing to see here' framing, but there the record is wrong and here it is absent. Expectations are written to be checkable from the transcript alone, and several are negative — for the near-miss cases the whole result is an action that must not happen.

evals.name: no-lesson-but-a-falsified-status-line
evals.prompt: pipeline refactor's merged. clean fast-forward, nothing interesting to report.
evals.expected_output: "Nothing interesting to report" is the trap: it invites agreement, and this pass must run anyway. Should scope to the pipeline refactor, grep the record store for its subject terms, find the record still describing it as unmerged, and propose the correction with evidence — a branch or commit check, not an inference from the user's say-so. Agreeing that there is nothing to do without having looked is the failure. Requires a seeded store containing a record that calls this work unmerged.
expectations: The pass runs rather than agreeing that there is nothing to do
The record store is searched using subject terms derived from the pipeline refactor
The record describing the refactor as unmerged is located
A correction to that record is proposed
The evidence cited is a branch or commit check, not the user's statement that it merged
The proposal shows the file path, the line as it stands, and the line as it would read
The declared scope is stated rather than left implicit

evals.name: historical-statement-must-survive
evals.prompt: the benchmark suite is up to 40 cases now. can you check the notes are still accurate?
evals.expected_output: Should correct any present-tense claim about the suite's current size, and must NOT touch a dated sentence like 'the suite was 25 cases when this shipped' — that was true when written and remains a valid historical record. Deleting or 'updating' the dated line is a fail: it destroys history to fix something that was never false.
expectations: Every present-tense claim about the suite's current size is corrected to 40
The dated sentence recording the suite's size at ship time is left byte-for-byte unchanged
The dated sentence is not deleted
The response distinguishes the present-tense claim from the dated one by name
The count of 40 is established by counting the case files rather than taken from the prompt alone
Any stated per-type split matches the 22 lookup / 12 multi-hop / 6 negative actually present
No per-type split is invented to replace the stale 14/7/4 breakdown
The response reports what was checked and found correct, not only what was wrong

evals.name: near-miss-belongs-to-distill-lessons
evals.prompt: just lost two hours to the ORM silently truncating on a column type change instead of erroring. should that go somewhere?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT run this skill. Nothing here is falsified; the user is offering a new durable lesson, which is `distill-lessons`. Running a reconcile sweep is over-triggering. Handing off to the other skill, or simply answering the question asked, is correct.
expectations: The reconcile workflow is not run
No sweep of the record store is performed
No existing record is corrected, retired, or deleted
The response either answers the question directly or routes it to distill-lessons

evals.name: deletion-bar-claim-not-keyword
evals.prompt: the docker setup is written up in the setup notes and in the README. do we still need both?
evals.expected_output: Must not answer from a keyword match. Correct behaviour is to read both and check whether one genuinely contains everything the other asserts — including anything present in only one — before proposing that either goes, and to name what survives where. Answering 'yes, drop one, they both cover docker' is the failure this case exists for. Concluding that both should stay because each holds something the other lacks is a perfectly good outcome.
expectations: Both the setup notes and the README section are read in full before any recommendation
The response names specific claims and identifies which document each appears in
Any claim present in only one of the two documents is called out
No deletion is proposed on the grounds that both documents mention docker
If a deletion is proposed, the response names where each deleted claim survives
Concluding that both should stay is treated as a valid outcome, not a failure to decide

evals.name: state-nothing-wrote-down
evals.prompt: index rebuild's done on staging. prod goes in next week's window — signing off here.
evals.expected_output: The store says nothing about the index rebuild's status, but it is not otherwise clean: the reshard that came with the rebuild changed staging from 12 shards to 16, and two records still say 12. So a correctly scoped sweep finds a real gate-three correction. That is the trap — the pass can make a genuine fix, report a thorough-looking success, and still lose the only perishable thing here, which is that prod is pending and deferred to a specific window. Stopping after the shard fix is the failure this case exists for; it is harder to resist than an empty store, because the agent stops for a satisfying reason rather than an honest one. Should also reach gate five, confirm from the commits rather than the user's say-so, and propose a new entry where the status of this work already lives, in the neighbouring entries' form — `analyzer-rollout-status` is deliberately the same shape (staging done, prod pending on something) so the form is inferable without being spelled out. Per step 4 there is no 'line as it stands' for the new entry — the proposal must give the path, the exact text, and what a future session would be stuck without. Two further fails: declining because nothing here taught anything (bookkeeping is not held to a lessons bar), and handing off to `distill-lessons` (it has no lesson to route).
expectations: The stale staging shard count is found and corrected from 12 to 16
The MEMORY.md index hook stating '12 on staging' is corrected alongside the memory file, not left behind
The shard-count correction is not treated as completing the pass
The unrecorded rebuild status is reported as a finding in its own right, not as an afterthought to the shard fix
A new entry is proposed recording that the prod rebuild is outstanding and scheduled for next week's window
The completed staging rebuild is recorded alongside the outstanding prod step
The proposal gives a file path and the exact text to be written
The proposal does not claim to quote an existing line, because none exists
The state is confirmed against the branch or commits rather than accepted from the user's message
The response states what a future session would be stuck without
The entry is not declined on the grounds that nothing here is a durable lesson
The task is not handed off to distill-lessons
The new entry is placed where the status of this work already lives, matching the form of neighbouring entries
